capabilities: Annotate selected passages with numbered highlights and comments
Queue annotations and send them with the next terminal message
Share the active note, selection, and open tabs with agents via their IDE integrations
Embed images in annotation comments saved to the attachment folder
Review, jump to, edit, or remove pending annotations from a panel
disambiguation: Not a Markdown formatting tool; 'markup' here means highlighting and annotating passages to share with AI agents.
extras: Marked as not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; the README states it makes no network requests, relies on undocumented agent IDE protocols that may break, and Windows support is untested.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to pass annotated passages, the current selection, and open-tab context to CLI coding agents so you can ask about specific text without pasting it.

relations.evidence: The Terminal plugin, to run the agents inside Obsidian and to get the panel.
Claude Code and Codex see the active note, the selected text and the open tabs through their own IDE integrations (/ide).
Codex needs /ide once per session. Its footer shows IDE context when it is on.

summary: Annotation plugin that highlights selected passages, attaches comments, and sends them with your selection to Claude Code or Codex running in an Obsidian terminal.
